title: Smooth connected closed subgroups of a semiabelian group are semiabelian
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. Let $G/k$ be a smooth separated commutative group scheme of finite type [def-pc-scheme, def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism] with semiabelian geometric fibres [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres]. Let $j:B\hookrightarrow G$ be a closed subgroup scheme [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup] such that $B$ is smooth over $k$ and connected [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-connected-scheme]. Then there are an integer $r\geq0$, an abelian variety $A/k$ [def-sc-abelian-variety], and homomorphisms $i:(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r\to B$ and $q:B\to A$ such that $i$ identifies the split torus [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type] with the scheme-theoretic kernel of $q$ and $q$ is locally surjective for the big fppf topology [def-pc-fppf-site]. Thus $1\to(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r\to B\to A\to1$ is exact as fppf sheaves. Rank zero and the trivial subgroup are allowed.

source.place: Corollary 3.2 and its application in Corollary 3.3, printed p.8. WANTED local archive; author PDF read online at https://math.stanford.edu/~conrad/DarmonCM/2011Notes/SemistableReduction.pdf . No SGA source is used.

proof.text: Apply [def-sfb-semiabelian-geometric-fibres] to the identity geometric point $\operatorname{Spec}k\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. It supplies $u:T_0=(\mathbf G_{m,k})^n\to G$ and $v:G\to A_0$, with $A_0$ an abelian variety and $u$ identifying $T_0$ with $\ker v$. The identity base change is identified with $G$ by its fibre-product universal property.

source.place: Theorem 8.27, Proposition 8.1(b), Example 8.4 and Definition 12.14; the subgroup argument of Conrad Corollary 3.2 (online author PDF, printed p.8).

proof.text: The closed immersion $j:B\to G$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](c), hence separated and of finite type by the definition of proper. The same node's clause (e) gives separatedness of $B\to\operatorname{Spec}k$; [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1) gives finite type. Smoothness and connectedness of $B$ are hypotheses. Apply [lem-sfb-barsotti-chevalley-decomposition] to obtain $a:L\hookrightarrow B$ and $p:B\to C$ with $L$ smooth connected affine, $C$ an abelian variety, $L=\ker p$ and $p$ fppf-locally surjective.

source.place: Theorem 8.27, Proposition 8.1(b), Example 8.4 and Definition 12.14; the subgroup argument of Conrad Corollary 3.2 (online author PDF, printed p.8).

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-affine-to-abelian-hom-vanishing] to the homomorphism $v\circ j\circ a:L\to A_0$. Its source is smooth connected affine of finite type by step 2, and its target is the abelian variety of step 1. It is zero. The universal property of $\ker v=G\times_{A_0}\operatorname{Spec}k$ therefore gives a homomorphism $h:L\to T_0$ with $u\circ h=j\circ a$. Its compatibility with multiplication follows by composing the two candidate multiplication maps with the monomorphism $u$ and cancelling $u$.

source.place: Theorem 8.27, Proposition 8.1(b), Example 8.4 and Definition 12.14; the subgroup argument of Conrad Corollary 3.2 (online author PDF, printed p.8).

proof.text: The map $h:L\to T_0$ is a closed immersion. Indeed, under $T_0=\ker v$, the square with horizontal arrows $h:L\to T_0$ and $j\circ a:L\to G$, and vertical arrows $\mathrm{id}_L$ and $u$, is Cartesian: on every test scheme $U$, a pair $(l,t)$ with $j(a(l))=u(t)$ has the unique solution $t=h(l)$ since $u$ is a monomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp], $j\circ a$ is a closed immersion, and by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change] its pullback $h$ is one. Thus $L$ is a smooth connected closed subgroup of the torus $T_0$. Apply [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus] to conclude that $L$ is a torus. Over the algebraically closed field $k$ this means there is a group-scheme isomorphism $b:(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r\simeq L$ for some $r\geq0$ [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type].

source.place: Theorem 8.27, Proposition 8.1(b), Example 8.4 and Definition 12.14; the subgroup argument of Conrad Corollary 3.2 (online author PDF, printed p.8).

proof.text: Set $A=C$, $q=p$ and $i=a\circ b$. Since $b$ is an isomorphism and $a$ identifies $L$ with $\ker p$, $i$ identifies the split torus with $\ker q$. The fppf local surjectivity of $p$ from step 2 is unchanged. These are exactly the two required exactness conditions. If $L=1$, choose $r=0$; the same construction works for $B=1$.

source.place: Theorem 8.27, Proposition 8.1(b), Example 8.4 and Definition 12.14; the subgroup argument of Conrad Corollary 3.2 (online author PDF, printed p.8).

Milne iAG2017 confirms Thm 8.27 with Note 8.30 (pp.154-155), Prop 8.1(b) and Ex 8.4 (p.149); Conrad is WANTED and not archived, so the proof is correctly marked agent-written. The item statement is true (Conrad Cor 3.2) and unchanged, and there is no re-split note. Step 1 applies the semiabelian-fibres definition at the identity geometric point. Step 2 gets B separated and of finite type from closed-immersion properness, separated composition and finite-type composition, then applies the Chevalley node. Step 3: the vanishing node makes v∘j∘a zero, so the map factors through ker v = T_0 by the fibre-product definition of the kernel in def-sc-group-scheme. Step 4: the square is Cartesian because u is a monomorphism, so h is the base change of a closed immersion; then the largest-subtorus node's last clause (a smooth connected closed subgroup of a torus is a torus) applies. Step 5 is elementary. New nodes: barsotti-chevalley-decomposition is Milne 8.27 over k=k̄, with fppf surjectivity coming from the faithfully flat quotient; affine-to-abelian-hom-vanishing is Milne 8.1(b) plus 8.4, and it needs smooth and connected (α_p and μ_n inside E show this) and has both. Neither node restates the item. Duplicate search over the snapshot DAG (chevalley, barsotti, affine/abelian, rigidity, semiabelian) found none; torus-abelian-hom-vanishing is a special case only. The four tool_uses are generic Mathlib-leaf scheme lemmas and are accepted. Batch-5 finding: lem-trf-smooth-fpqc-base-descent is a Mathlib leaf (Stacks 02VL, smoothness descends along flat quasi-compact surjections). It is generic descent, given by neither assumption and not a step of their proofs, so it is outside the assumed statements and accepted.

lean.statement: theorem smooth_connected_semiabelian_subgroup (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (G : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) [IsCommMonObj G.X] [Smooth G.X.hom] [IsSeparated G.X.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.X.hom] [QuasiCompact G.X.hom] (hG : HasSemiabelianGeometricFibres G) (B : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (j : B ⟶ G) [IsClosedSubgroupScheme j.hom.hom] [Smooth B.X.hom] [ConnectedSpace B.X.left] : ∃ (r : ℕ) (A : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) (i : MultiplicativeType.splitTorus k r ⟶ B) (q : B ⟶ A), IsAbelianVariety A.X ∧ IsPullback i.hom.hom (toUnit (MultiplicativeType.splitTorus k r).X) q.hom.hom η[A.X] ∧ Presheaf.IsLocallySurjective (Scheme.fppfTopology.over (Spec (.of k))) (yoneda.map q.hom.hom)
